statements.action_statement: Upgrade to crawl4ai 0.8.0 once available in conda-forge. In the interim, users running the Docker API server should either disable the API, block the `/crawl` endpoint at the network or firewall level, or add authentication in front of it. Users consuming crawl4ai purely as a Python library (not running the Docker API server) are not directly reachable via this attack vector but should still upgrade when the fix lands.
statements.status_notes: Both advisories supplied are identical duplicates of GHSA-5882-5rx9-xgxp; a single assessment covers both. The conda-forge feedstock maintainer should track the 0.8.0 PyPI release and expedite the recipe bump given the CRITICAL rating. The `affects_future: True` flag should be cleared once 0.8.0 is published to conda-forge.

statements.action_statement: No patched mlflow-pipelines release exists on conda-forge. Users should either restrict the tracking server to localhost or a trusted VPN segment, or migrate to the mainline mlflow conda-forge package at >= 2.5.0. Directory traversal payloads can reach this endpoint without authentication, so network-level controls are the only mitigation available at this version.
statements.status_notes: Both CVE-2023-6015 and CVE-2023-3765 affect the same server component at overlapping version ranges. A single upgrade to >= 2.8.1 (the higher of the two fix versions) would remediate both. The conda-forge mlflow-pipelines feedstock should be flagged for EOL or migration guidance.

statements.action_statement: No fixed version of mlflow-pipelines is available on conda-forge (latest is 1.30.0, fix requires >= 2.8.1). Users should restrict network access to the MLflow tracking server to trusted hosts only, or migrate to the mainline mlflow conda-forge package at a version >= 2.8.1. Avoid exposing the tracking server on untrusted or public networks.
statements.status_notes: Since mlflow-pipelines on conda-forge appears to be pinned at the 1.x series with no further releases, there is effectively no upgrade path within this conda package. Maintainers should consider EOL-marking the feedstock or redirecting users to the mainline mlflow conda-forge package.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow to >= 2.9.2 by migrating to the mlflow-recipes conda package (the 2.x successor to mlflow-pipelines). Until upgraded, restrict network access to the MLflow tracking server to trusted, authenticated clients only.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2023-6018 and CVE-2023-6831 are both present simultaneously in mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 and share the same fix release (2.9.2). Neither can be patched within the mlflow-pipelines 1.x conda line; full remediation requires migrating to mlflow-recipes on conda-forge.

statements.action_statement: Upgrade mlflow to >= 2.9.2 by migrating to the mlflow-recipes conda package, which is the 2.x successor to mlflow-pipelines. Do not expose the MLflow tracking server to untrusted networks until the upgrade is complete.
statements.status_notes: GHSA-554w-xh4j-8w64 and GHSA-5p3h-7fwh-92rc were both fixed in the 2.9.2 release and share the same remediation path; mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 users are simultaneously exposed to both. The conda-forge mlflow-pipelines feedstock has been effectively abandoned at 1.30.0 with no planned future releases.

The OSV 'introduced: 0' range appears to be an over-classification that should be corrected to 'introduced: 2.2.0'. A maintainer may want to flag this upstream to the OSV/GitHub Advisory Database. The mlflow-pipelines conda package is not affected by this CVE and should be excluded from any automated patch-urgency workflows triggered by GHSA-5q6c-ffvg-xcm9.

The discrepancy between the OSV 'introduced: 0' range event and the advisory text 'affects versions 3.8.0' should be flagged to the OSV maintainers or the GitHub Advisory Database for correction. The auto-match pipeline should be reviewed for over-broad OSV range events where the advisory narrative provides a tighter bound. No action is required for the mlflow-pipelines 1.30.0 conda artifact with respect to this CVE.
